posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
Envisioner:

Sigh, once again the purity of art is quashed in order to pander to the wishes of a few (in this case ONE) persons who place their own feelings as being more important than others' freedom of expression.  I'm not surprised, I'm just disappointed.

  1. The pentagram with one point up is the Elder Sign, a symbol associated with Nightmist and dark stuff and thus is actually probably a better fit for Infernal damage than the inverted pentagram.

  2. No offense to Greater Than Games or the team at Handelabra, but I would hesitate to refer to the choice of which way to orient a pentagram to represent a certain type of damage in an app used to track the current state of a card game 'art'.

  3. At no point did Dryden make any kind of demands about this, nor did he try to place himself above other people's freedom of expression. He made a polite request, ignored the troll whose solution was 'don't look at it lol', and was heard by Christopher and MigrantP, who decided to make a single very minor change in order to keep at least one (and quite possibly more) fans happy. Where exactly is the quashing in all this?

 

Personally, I think being offended by a particular symbol a little silly, but I find being offended by customer service patently absurd.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
BlueHairedMeerkat:
  1. The pentagram with one point up is the Elder Sign, a symbol associated with Nightmist and dark stuff and thus is actually probably a better fit for Infernal damage than the inverted pentagram.

An elder sign is not a pentagram.  It's a weirdly asymmetrical 5-pointed star with no surrounding circle, and a small flame-eye symbol in the middle.

  1. At no point did Dryden make any kind of demands about this, nor did he try to place himself above other people's freedom of expression. He made a polite request, ignored the troll whose solution was 'don't look at it lol'

So because he was "polite", I'm somehow a troll?  Apparently my feelings don't matter just because I got angrier than he did.  Personally I would have thought that meant I felt more strongly about the situation and thus deserve at least as much consideration.

and was heard by Christopher and MigrantP, who decided to make a single very minor change in order to keep at least one (and quite possibly more) fans happy. Where exactly is the quashing in all this? Personally, I think being offended by a particular symbol a little silly, but I find being offended by customer service patently absurd.

Customer service is great, as long as it applies to all customers equally.  But the "quashing" would be the fact that the opinions of people who think pentagrams are offensive are being valued, and the opinions of people who think crosses are offensive are not, just because there are more of the former.  (Admittedly, there are a lot more crosses in card art.  And at no point did I suggest they should be removed, but I do in fact consider them offensive; I'm just not of the opinion that any person has a right to censor reality for the sake of their prejudices.)

Christopher is making Dryden more happy, but me less so, and in either case, he isn't preserving the purity of the original work, but rather changing it to pander to anyone who raises an issue.  I don't consider that to be admirable behavior.  When Harlan Ellison's writing offends someone, he takes pride in it, because that's the point of writing, to challenge people's beliefs and force them to rethink their worldview.  Yes Sentinels is a fun game, but it's also more than that, and its gravity and dignity should be respected, even over the wishes of its own creators (the trope name for this is "Death of the Author"…because the author will eventually die, his own interpretation of his works is no more important than any other interpretation, for the work must be able to stand on its own).
